source.title: Sparsity, Superposition, and Forgetting: A Mechanistic Study of Representation Retention in Continual Learning
source.authors: Jan Wasilewski; Jȩdrzej Kozal; Micha l Woźniak; Bartosz Krawczyk

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures synthetic feature-direction overlap and retention, but it does not test neuron-pole interpretability, the audit percentages, the named model or architectures, attribution graphs, or explanation-scoring claims in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own results about superposition and feature retention in a controlled toy continual-learning setup. These do not measure any claim version's specified outcome; the relevant qualitative findings are recorded under fits_no_version. Effective-rank results are not included because they do not bear on the claim's stated subject.
record.test_reason: A toy continual-learning study of ground-truth feature directions (overlap, representation strength, retention) in a small replay-trained encoder. It does not measure neuron-level interpretability shares, polysemantic neuron examples, architecture or tool effects on interpretable-neuron share, neuron attribution graphs, or explanation scoring. It mentions superposition and polysemantic neurons only as background, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that sparsity drives overlap, with dips at task boundaries. Overlap harms retention mainly when representations are weak. Effective rank rises with sparsity. Strength and capacity allocation, not overlap alone, moderate forgetting.
record.recipe_differences: The study probes synthetic ground-truth features in a replay-trained toy encoder and measures directional overlap and retention; it does not audit or score neuron explanations.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported qualitative results are described across sparsity regimes and alternative settings; SINDy coefficient selection varies across runs, while the sign structure of dominant interactions is reported as stable.

fits_no_version.finding: In a toy bottlenecked encoder, sparser synthetic features show larger directional overlap S(i,t) (Fig. 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparser ground-truth features are encoded with more superposition in a capacity-limited toy encoder during continual learning.

fits_no_version.finding: Superposition dips at task boundaries, then recovers and grows. Retention loss concentrates on weak, highly overlapped, recently introduced features (Figs. 3–4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Overlap's link to representation loss in toy continual learning is moderated by representation strength and time since first exposure.

record.problems: The study is intentionally limited to a controlled toy setting with synthetic features and disjoint task supports. Its retention measure tracks representation-strength changes rather than classifier performance, and the main reported results are qualitative rather than accompanied here by numerical effect sizes or uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results were left out. Task effective-rank findings in Figures 5 and 6 were omitted because they do not measure any listed claim version or the claim's stated subject.

untested.parts: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit and its shares (90%/7%/2–4%).
Shares in other dense or MoE language models and at scale.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron; pose feature; recursive generalization versus superposition.
Architecture, regularization and tool effects on the share of interpretable neurons.
Neuron-based attribution graphs without a replacement model.
Whether explanations from activating examples predict firing.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only'. The paper only uses superposition and polysemanticity as background framing (Elhage et al., Olah et al.) and makes no argument about any version. Its 'features' are ground-truth latent directions, not neurons, so the rows rightly carry no version links. The effective-rank results (RQ3) were also correctly left out.

versions.untested_parts: The Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit and all stated proportions.
Other language models, dense or mixture-of-experts architectures, and scaling up to trillions of parameters.
The InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, shared pose features, and recursive generalization versus superposition.
Architecture, regularization, interpretability tools, and the estimates for InceptionV1-sized vision models.
Attribution graphs, behavioral explanation by a model's own neurons, and reconstruction error.
Whether explanations based on activating examples predict where neurons fire.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: controlled framework encoder (model name not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Measured feature-direction overlap (superposition strength) for pure-feature probes across sparsity regimes.
rows.measure: Superposition strength S(i,t), defined by squared projections of other feature embeddings onto the feature's unit direction.
rows.value: The text reports systematically larger S(i,t) for sparser features.
rows.note: The paper uses ground-truth synthetic features and a toy encoder, not neuron poles or human-interpretable jobs.

rows.subject: controlled framework encoder (model name not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked feature superposition strength over sequential training time.
rows.measure: Temporal pattern of superposition strength S(i,t).
rows.value: The text reports a transient dip in superposition when a new task starts, followed by gradual recovery and continued growth.
rows.note: The result is described qualitatively across settings; numerical effect sizes are not stated.

rows.subject: controlled framework encoder (model name not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Related changes in representation strength and superposition to feature-retention dynamics using SINDy.
rows.measure: Retention F(i,t), the temporal derivative of representation strength.
rows.value: The text reports the most negative retention for weakly represented, highly overlapped features; stronger representations buffer overlap, and retention becomes closer to zero or slightly positive later after first exposure.
rows.note: This measures a synthetic feature-strength proxy, not neuron explanation accuracy or the share of interpretable neuron poles.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
